query: May I accept the riverworks collection for a first, limited intake?
target: Accept a review visit and up to two rights-cleared boxes, with no promise beyond that.
relation: The riverworks inspection episode defines a defensible first boundary, while the parish map intake episode shows why accepting the whole collection without counts and rights would repeat a storage failure.
A: When the riverworks folders arrived with decade labels but no item count, I told the donor committee we could schedule an inspection visit and accept up to two boxes after rights confirmations, not the whole collection.
B: Two years ago I accepted an entire parish map collection on a verbal promise of future inventory; within a month the stacks overflowed and public access hours were cut while we counted unsorted material.
E1: The archive has an empty flat-file cabinet and two volunteers available on alternate Saturdays.
E2: The annual exhibition programme is printed in three months.
B_prime: The donor committee agreed to an inspection visit but wants every box accepted before rights confirmations are requested.
lure: A councillor says announcing the entire collection would attract visitors to the exhibition.

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the collection log and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The donor folder review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I accepted a club photograph donation once the numbered inventory and signed permission arrived.
Was the collection fully described?
Yes, every item and public-use limit was listed.
Someone new shadowed me in the archive studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the intake months into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.

When the riverworks folders arrived with decade labels but no item count, I told the donor committee we could schedule an inspection visit and accept up to two boxes after rights confirmations, not the whole collection.
What could not be planned from the inventory?
Storage demand, cataloguing effort, and any public display schedule.
I logged a returned folder after a donor supplied the missing accession note.
Did that change intake scope?
No, it completed one record already on the shelf.
I archived last cycle's notes on the donor folder and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The archive has an empty flat-file cabinet and two volunteers available on alternate Saturdays.
Does that support unrestricted intake?
No, it supports an initial review and a small selected transfer.
A vendor call about the collection log ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the archive studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the intake months.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the donor folder records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.

Two years ago I accepted an entire parish map collection on a verbal promise of future inventory; within a month the stacks overflowed and public access hours were cut while we counted unsorted material.
What was missing at acceptance?
A counted inventory and confirmed rights before anything crossed the threshold.
I sketched next week's plan for the intake months before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the collection log updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The annual exhibition programme is printed in three months.
Does that force a display promise?
No, the programme can describe the work as under review.
I compared two options for the donor folder tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the archive studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
